* * *
 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.2,00,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Sri.Jayanth B K who met with road traffic accident.

Brief facts of the petitioners case is as follows:
2.

That on 11-06-2024 at about 11-30 pm., Jayanth B K along with his friend Shasidaran as a pedestrian, was crossing Mysore- Bangalore road and when they reached in front of Empire hotel to go towards their car for their onward journey towards Hunsur town, at that time the driver of Motor Car bearing Reg.No.KL-10-AK-2288 came from Mysore direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the above said persons, result of which Jayanth sustained grievous injuries and Shasidaran died at the spot.
Immediately Jayanth B K was shifted to D R M Hospital at Mandya and further treatment at DRM Hospital, Mysore, but during the course of treatment, Jayanth B K succumbed to the injuries on 12-06-2024.

entities.text: D R M Hospital at Mandya
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: So far, the petitioners have spent sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses and Rs.2,00,000/- towards funeral and obsequies ceremony.
3. Prior to the accident, Jayanth B K was hale and healthy.
He was doing business and earning sum of Rs.1,00,000/- p.m.
Due to the sudden death of Jayanth B K., the petitioners have suffered mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

4. The respondent no.1/the RC owner of Motor Car bearing Reg.No.KL-10-AK-2288 has filed written statement and contended that Motor Car bearing Reg.No.KL-10-AK-2288 was insured with the respondent no.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.

It was further contended that he had valid driving licence as on the date of accident and that the alleged accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of Jayanth B K who without following the traffic rules and regulations had crossed the road at the place where there was no zebra crossing.
5.

Respondent no.2 /the Motor Car bearing Reg.No.KL-10-AK-2288 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the rider of the insured vehicle was not holding valid driving license and that accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself who without observing the vehicle movement had suddenly rushed to the road in order to cross the road and came in contact with the insured vehicle, hence the driver of the insured has not contributed any amount of negligence.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Issues that would arise for my consideration as follows:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Jayanth B K succumbed to the injuries sustained in a Motor Vehicle accident, that occurred on 11- 06-2024 at about 11-30 pm., on Bangalore -Mysore road, Infront of Empire Hotel, Chennapatna Taluk, Ramanagara, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Motor Car bearing Reg.No.KL-10-AK-2288?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7.
The petitioner No.1 got examined herself as Pw1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P19.

On the other hand, Respondent No.2 has examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.
8.
Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondents and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above Points are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-

sentences.text: Issue No.1:

Petitioners have categorically contended that on 11-06-2024 at about 11-30 to 11.50 p.m., Jayanth B K (here in after called the deceased) as a pedestrian, was standing to cross B.M Road, near Empire Hotel along with his friend Shashidaharan.

K, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-10-AK- 2288 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the pedestrian ie., Jayanth B K result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

11. In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.1 who is the wife of the deceased got examined herself as Pw1 and produced in all 13 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.P3 Ex.P5 to Ex.P12 i.e., FIR with complaint, PM report, Inquest report, Charge sheet, Spot Mahazar, Sketch,
Statement of witness, Seizure mahazar with photographs of the damaged vehicle and deceased,
Police intimation, police memo, statement of accused are the material documents to prove the present issue.

12. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Rajashekhar, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0096/2024 of Channapatna Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC.

The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279,
337, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.177, 179 of MV Act.

13. The Learned counsel for respondent no2 has seriously disputed the allegation made by the petitioners against the driver of the offending vehicle stating that the driver of the offending vehicle has contributed sole negligence.

It is vehemently submitted that the deceased had crossed the road at the place where there was no provision to cross and deceased had crossed the road against to the traffic rules hence only abated charge sheet was filed even against the deceased u/Sec. 177, 179 of IMV Act along with other Sections under the IPC.
14.

If the police records are perused, it is true that though the complaint was lodged against the driver of the offending vehicle but after investigation charge sheet was filed even against the deceased.
It is not in dispute that at the time of accident, deceased was crossing the National Highway ie., Mysore - Bengaluru road.
It is further not in dispute that at the time of accident offending vehicle was proceeding from Mysore towards Bangalore.
It is a double road of the width of nearly 40 feet.
There is a divider in between two roads.
The spot of accident is on the extreme right side of Mysore _ Bengaluru Highway.
It is true that since Mysore- Bengaluru is one way road, the vehicles are plying in the said road from Mysore towards Bangalore.

Hence, when the width of the road is sufficiently wide to an extent of 40 feet, the driver of the offending vehicle could have drive his vehicle on the left side of the side road but he took the vehicle towards extreme right side of the road touching to the divider and hit to the deceased who was standing by the side of the divider.

As observed supra, respondent no.1 has vehemently contended that the place at which deceased had crossed the road is a restricted area wherein pedestrian/publics were prohibited from crossing the road.
15. But this court is of the opinion that pedestrians are strictly prohibited from crossing the road provided there is other provision to cross the road.

It is true that crossing dangerously or in Rashmi K S vs Rashid on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104656211/

Pedestrians do not have an absolute right to cross any where at any time, they have a right to safe passage.
The passengers have to use designated areas due to the high risk of fatal accidents.

Though the respondent no.2 has stated that the place at which deceased had crossed the road is a restricted area and that there is no zebra crossing, but no suggestion was posed to the PW.1 that the deceased had crossed the road where there is no zebra crossing.

Further the deceased had already crossed the road and he was standing near the divider, under such circumstances had the driver driven his vehicle with all care and caution on the left side of the road without taking the vehicle on the extreme right side of the road this accident would not have occurred.
At the same time, crossing the road dangerously in the National Highway is also to be avoided.

16. Now in order to assess the percentage of negligence contributed by the deceased and the driver of the offending vehicle, it is better to have glance on the judgment reported in ILR 1998 Kar 1934 between Sri Narasimhaiah Vs. The General Manager & Anr.,

sentences.text: In the said case, pedestrian had crossed the road at a point where he ought not to have crossed the road.
The Hon'ble High Court by observing that petitioner too has contributed negligence has fixed ratio of 40 as negligence contributed by the petitioner.

17. In an un-reported judgment rendered in MFA No. 7070/2015 (MV) between Smt.Mina Limbu &
Ors., Vs., M/s Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd., it was held by referring the facts of the case that "pedestrian crossing the road at a point where he ought not to have done, it has to be considered that pedestrian too has contributed negligence.

Ors., Vs., M/s Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd.

sentences.text: In the said case, 25% of negligence was attributed against the deceased.

18. In MFA NO.2380/2016 between Smt. Gangamma Vs., Sri. Vardharaju & Anr., in the said case also referring some of the judgment rendered by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it has observed that "where the person is crossing the road where there was no zebra crossing and accident occurs,
some percentage of negligence has to be attributed against the person who crossed the road and met with an accident".

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, 20% negligence was attributed against the deceased.

19. In the present case, considering the fact that deceased was standing near the divider and the driver of the offending vehicle took the vehicle on the extreme right side of the road and hit to the deceased who was standing on the extreme right side of the road, the negligence contributed by the deceased can be assessed at 15% and the negligence contributed by the driver of the offending vehicle is assessed at the ratio of 85%
Hence, petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 15%.
Accordingly issue no.1 is answered in Partly Affirmative.
20. Issue No 2:

It is the contention taken by the petitioners that, petitioner No.1 being the wife,
petitioner no.2 being the minor son and petitioner No.3 being the mother of the deceased are entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased and that deceased was doing business and agriculture and earning Rs.1,00,000/- p.m.
21.
It is stated by the petitioners that at the time of accident deceased was aged about 34 years.

The petitioners have produced Aadhaar card of the deceased which reflects the date of birth of deceased Rashmi K S vs Rashid on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104656211/
5 as 03-01-1990.
As the accident in question has taken place in the year 2024, it can be said that the deceased was aged about 34 years as on the date of accident.
22. As observed earlier, it is contended by the petitioners that deceased was doing business and agriculture and earning Rs.1,00,000/- p.m.

To substantiate the said contention petitioners have produced Income Tax Returns for the year 2020-2021, 2022-2023 and 2023-2024 at Ex.P4.
23.
If the IT returns for the assessment year 2020-2021 to 2023-2024 is perused, during the Assessment year 2020-2021 the gross income of the deceased from his business was Rs.4,40,800/-.
During the Assessment year 2020-2021 the gross income of the deceased was Rs.4,57,080/-.
In the Assessment year 2022-2023 the total income of the deceased was Rs.4,69,970/-.
In the assessment year 2023-2024 the gross income of the deceased was Rs.4,90,670/-.
If the average income of the deceased from the business for the three assessment year is considered, then the annual income of the deceased would come to Rs.4,72,574/-

The calculation is as follows:
Income of the year 2020-2022 is Rs 4,57,080/- Income of the year 2022-2023 is Rs.4,69,970/-
Income of the year 2023-2024 is Rs 4,90,670/-

If average three years income is taken, it comes as follows:
Rs.4,57,080/- + Rs.4,69,970/- + Rs.4,90,670 = Rs.14,17,720/-.

If Rs.14,17,720/- is divided by 3 it comes around Rs.4,72,574/- which is the annual income of the deceased and if the said annual income is converted into monthly income it comes to Rs.39,381/-.
24.
The petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner no.2 being the minor son and petitioner No.3 being the mother of the deceased are the dependents of the deceased.

25. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife, son and mother, 1/3rd of the annual income is to be deducted towards the personal expenses and remaining 2/3rd is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.
26.

Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40%
of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case, as deceased was aged around 34 years, 40% should be added towards future prospects.

6 27.

Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.39,381/-, by adding 40% towards future prospect it comes to Rs.55,133/-, out of it if 1/3rd is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.36,756/-
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 31 to 34 is '16'.

Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.70,57,152/-
(Rs.36,756/- x 16 x 12 =70,57,152/-).

28. Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 lost her husband, petitioner No.2 lost his beloved father and petitioner no.3 lost her son in her old age, thereby lost the love and affection of deceased.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium,
towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/-
and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

29. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.

Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.
30.
In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:

Under the heads Amount  ( in rupees )
 1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/-
 2 Transportation and funeral Rs. 18,150/-
 expenses  3 Loss of spousal consortium, Rs. 1,45,200/-
 parental consortium and  filial consortium  (Rs.48,400x3)
4 Loss of dependency Rs. 70,57,152/-

Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.79,38,652/- and it is just and adequate compensation Rashmi K S vs Rashid on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104656211/
7 under the facts and circumstances of the case.
31. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with the 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Since both deceased and the driver of the offending vehicle had contributed negligence to the extent of 15:85 this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount,
petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 15%.
The respondent no.2 being the insurer is liable to pay 85% of the awarded compensation to the petitioners.
85% of the compensation shall carry interest at 6% p.a.
Accordingly issue no 2 is answered.
32. Issue No.4 :- In the light of findings given on Issue No. 2 and 3 , my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.79,38,652/- (Rupees Seventy Nine Lakhs Thirty Eight Thousand Six Hundred Fifty Two only)

The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay 85% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.67,47,854/- (Rupees Sixty Seven Lakhs Forty Seven Thousand Eight Hundred Fifty Four only) with interest there on at 6% within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Petitioners shall forgo 15% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.11,90,798/-
Out of the compensation amount
, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs. 40,00,000/- Petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs. 19,00,000/- Petitioner No.3 is entitled for Rs. 8,47,854/-

Out of the amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 and 3 shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioners on proper identification.

Entire compensation amount is ordered to be deposited in the name of minor petitioner no.2 till he attains the age of majority reserving right to the petitioner no.1 to withdrawn the accrued interest for the maintenance and welfare of the minor.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
